navigation: EFLS LiDAR+ (solid-state LiDAR + Network RTK + Vision)
use_cases: Mid-large residential lawns up to 0.5 acre

name: Navimow X315
desc: X-series commercial Navimow for large properties (~1500m²). Vision + RTK navigation, multi-zone scheduling, anti-theft features.

name: Navimow X330
desc: Larger X-series Navimow for 3000m² lawns. Vision + RTK navigation, commercial-grade.

name: Navimow X350
desc: X-series commercial Navimow with 4WD. 84% slope capability — class-leading. Zero-turn ORV-tuned chassis for damage-free mowing. Wire-free RTK + Vision.

name: Navimow X390
desc: Larger 4WD Navimow X-series for 0.95-acre lawns. Same 84% slope capability and ORV-tuned chassis as X350.

name: Navimow X430
desc: Navimow 2026 4WD flagship for 1-acre lawns. 84% slope, zero-turn ORV-tuned chassis. EFLS LiDAR+ triple-fusion navigation.

name: Navimow X450
desc: Larger sibling to X430 — 1.25 acres. Same 4WD + EFLS LiDAR+ stack.

name: GOAT G1
desc: Ecovacs first-generation GOAT (2023). Boundary-free with UWB beacon positioning + AI camera. Predecessor to the LiDAR PRO line.

name: GOAT GX-600
desc: Budget GOAT variant for 600m² lawns. Boundary-free with AI camera navigation. Entry into the GOAT family.

name: GOAT A2000 LiDAR PRO
desc: Mid-tier GOAT with dual-LiDAR auto-mapping for 0.5-acre lawns. Same TruEdge trimmer system as O1000. AIVI 3D obstacle avoidance.

name: GOAT A3000 LiDAR PRO
desc: Top-tier GOAT with 32V high-performance battery, dual blade-disc design, 400W max cutting power (3x efficiency vs standard). 3000m² coverage. Best Ecovacs for large complex yards. 400m²/h coverage rate.

name: GOAT O1000 LiDAR PRO
desc: Ecovacs entry-flagship 2026 wire-free mower for 1/4-acre lawns. HoloScope 360 Dual-LiDAR (mechanical 360° + 3D ToF solid-state) + AI camera, AIVI 3D obstacle avoidance (200+ types, 5cm precision). Built-in TruEdge trimmer for zero-edge cuts. 80cm narrow-path capability. IPX6.
use_cases: Compact residential lawns up to 0.3 acre

name: Landroid S WR165
desc: Compact Landroid for 1/8-acre lawns. Uses Worx 20V 2.0Ah Power Share battery (compatible with 35+ Worx tools). Floating blade disc auto-adjusts for uneven terrain. Patented AIA (Artificial Intelligence Algorithm) for narrow-passage navigation. Cut-to-Edge offset blades minimize trimming. Boundary wire required.
use_cases: Small residential lawns up to 1/8 acre

name: Landroid M WR147
desc: Mid-size Landroid for 1/4-acre lawns. Worx 20V 4.0Ah Power Share battery. Four wheels for traction. Same AIA navigation and floating blade as S series, with longer runtime.

name: Landroid L WR155
desc: Large Landroid for 1/2-acre lawns. Worx 20V 6.0Ah Power Share battery, 115-minute charge time. Cloud computing for auto-scheduling based on local weather, season, grass species and sun radiation. OTA updates.

name: Landroid Vision WR235
desc: Worx camera-vision Landroid — wire-free, no antenna or boundary wire. AI camera trained on grass recognition. Works under tree canopy where satellite navigation fails. Major shift from wire-bound traditional Landroids.

name: Landroid Vision Cloud M1000
desc: Worx 2026 Vision Landroid with cloud-based AI for adaptive mowing. Camera navigation, OTA model updates from the cloud, no boundary wire.

name: RTKn Mission Mega
desc: Kress (Positec) commercial RTKn mower — RTK without local antenna ('RTKn' = network RTK). Designed for large European lawns.

name: KR136E RTK
desc: Kress (Positec brand) wire-free robotic mower with RTK satellite navigation. Targets European market with 600m² coverage. Uses local RTK reference antenna for centimeter-level accuracy.

name: KR160E RTK
desc: Larger Kress RTK mower for 1000m² lawns. Same RTK + GPS navigation as KR136E.

name: OptiMow 15H
desc: Greenworks budget-tier robotic mower for 1500m² lawns. Boundary-wire installation, sensor-based obstacle detection.

name: OptiMow 50H
desc: Larger Greenworks robotic mower for 5000m² lawns. Boundary-wire installation, larger battery.

name: A1
desc: Dreame's first-generation A-series robot mower. RTK-Vision navigation, OmniSense 3D obstacle detection. Wire-free with antenna station.

name: A2
desc: Mid-2025 Dreame A2 with refined RTK-Vision and improved obstacle avoidance. 2000m² coverage.

name: A3 AWD
desc: Dreame A3 with AWD platform for steep slopes (75%). LiDAR + RTK + Vision triple-fusion. Up to 3000m².

name: A3 AWD Pro
desc: Top Dreame 2026 A3 AWD Pro with enhanced sensor stack, full LELS-like navigation, and largest battery in the series.

name: RockMow Z130
desc: Roborock's first lawn-mower line (announced 2026). RockMow Z130 brings the company's StarSight ToF navigation expertise to outdoor mowing. Wire-free.

name: RockMow X1 LiDAR
desc: Roborock RockMow X1 with solid-state LiDAR for wire-free large-lawn mowing. Larger sibling to Z130.

name: E18
desc: Eufy/Anker's first-generation robot mower. RTK + Vision navigation, wire-free. Targets mid-size US lawns.

name: LiDAX Ultra 1000
desc: MOVA (Dreame sub-brand) — RTK-free 360° 3D LiDAR + AI Vision auto-mapping for 1/4-acre lawns. Zero-edge cutting, 150 managed zones.

name: Sunseeker S4
desc: Sunseeker S4 LiDAR robot mower for 1000m² (0.25 acre) lawns. Vision AI + 360° 3D LiDAR navigation. Quiet 60dB operation, 42% slope handling.

name: Elite X4
desc: Sunseeker flagship — RTK + Vision wire-free mower for mid-to-large lawns. Compact European-style design.

name: Eyeon 500 AI-VISION
desc: Litheli budget vision-only mower for small lawns. No RTK, no boundary wire — pure AI camera navigation.

name: Skope 800 AI-VISION
desc: Litheli Skope 800 — vision-based robot mower for 800m² lawns. Wire-free, AI obstacle avoidance.

name: KEENMOW K1
desc: KEENON Robotics (known for hospitality service robots) entering outdoor robotics with KEENMOW K1. RTK + Vision navigation, commercial focus.

name: Lymow One Plus
desc: Lymow tracked-chassis robot mower — unusual track design for excellent slope and rough-terrain handling without wheel spin.

name: Tron Ultra
desc: Airseekers Tron Ultra — vision-based wire-free robot mower. New brand entering 2026 market with focus on small-to-mid lawns.

name: NAVIA 6000
desc: NexLawn flagship — newer entrant to the wire-free robotic mower market. RTK + Vision navigation, large-lawn coverage up to 6000m².

name: Goko M6
desc: RobotPlusPlus Goko M6 — wire-free robot mower from new entrant. Vision-based navigation.

name: Lawn Mower M1
desc: Yarbo's modular outdoor robot platform's lawn mower attachment. Same platform also snow-blows and leaf-blows. RTK + Vision.

name: G1 Autonomous Mower
desc: Pandag G1 autonomous lawn mower — newer entry to wire-free robot mower category.

name: Figure 03
desc: Figure AI's third-generation humanoid (unveiled October 2025). Built for the home alongside industrial deployment. Helix 2.0 vision-language-action model. Soft fabric exterior, mesh hair design. BMW Spartanburg production deployment for the Figure 02 fleet. Brett Adcock targets one million Figure 03 units across 4 years. Closed $1.5B Series C at $39.5B valuation Sept 2025.

name: Optimus Gen 3
desc: Tesla's third-generation Optimus, demonstrated 2026. Significant upgrade over Gen 2 — improved hands with biological-inspired tendon actuation, faster walking gait. Target: $25-30K consumer price at scale, with internal Tesla factory deployment first. Powered by Tesla Dojo training infrastructure.

name: Atlas (Hydraulic)
desc: Boston Dynamics' original hydraulic Atlas. DARPA Robotics Challenge platform (2013), evolved through HD Atlas (2016) which dropped from 330lb to 180lb. Famous for parkour, backflips, dance, gymnastics demonstrations 2017-2024. Retired April 2024 in favor of the all-electric Atlas. Powered by 28 hydraulic actuators. Historic — defined what humanoid robotics could be.

name: Atlas (Electric)
desc: Boston Dynamics' fifth-generation Atlas — fully electric replacement for the hydraulic original. Unveiled April 2024 after the hydraulic Atlas's retirement. Production debut at CES 2026 with $420K initial pricing. Custom 3D-printed titanium/aluminum actuators (Hyundai Mobis). 360° hip/waist/neck rotation impossible for humans. Designed for industrial deployment at Hyundai Metaplant. 56 DOF, 50 kg payload, 2.3m reach. Powered by DeepMind Gemini Robotics models via Orbit platform.

name: NEO
desc: 1X Technologies' consumer-ready home humanoid. Pre-orders opened October 2025 at $20,000 (or $499/month subscription). First US deliveries scheduled 2026. Soft 3D-lattice polymer exterior + lightweight composite frame + tendon-drive joints make it human-safe. 22-DoF hands per side (44 total) for human-level dexterity. 22 dB acoustic profile — quieter than a refrigerator. OpenAI-backed. Powered by Redwood AI (video-trained World Model). NVIDIA Jetson Thor compute.

name: A1
desc: AGIBOT's first humanoid product (Raise A1, August 2023 unveiling). Predecessor to the A2 line that propelled AGIBOT to #1 humanoid volume globally.

name: A2
desc: AGIBOT (Zhiyuan Robotics, Shanghai) flagship full-size humanoid. AGIBOT shipped ~5,168 humanoids in 2025 — the world's #1 humanoid producer by volume per Omdia analyst firm. Held Guinness World Record for 106km autonomous walk Suzhou-to-Shanghai. 40+ DOF, 200 TOPS AI compute, GO-1 vision-language foundation model. Multi-region certified (China, US, Europe). PLd safety architecture with 360° perception.

name: A3
desc: AGIBOT A3 (Expedition A3) — third-generation humanoid in development. Builds on A2 platform with refined dexterity and longer endurance.

name: H2
desc: AGIBOT H2 (Heavy 2) — industrial humanoid for heavy logistics, in development. Sister product to A2 Max.

name: X2-N Nezha
desc: AGIBOT X2-N Nezha — child-sized humanoid platform for compact applications. Named after the Chinese mythological figure.

name: Walker S1
desc: UBTECH's industrial humanoid deployed at BYD, Geely, Foxconn factories for quality inspection, material handling. 41 high-precision joints, intelligent collaborative inspection of multiple Walker S1 working together. AI BrainNet 'multi-brain collaborative network'.

name: Alpha 1E
desc: UBTECH consumer/educational mini-humanoid. Programmable via app for dancing, gestures, simple movements. Targeted STEM education and home entertainment.

name: IRON
desc: XPeng (EV manufacturer) IRON humanoid. Uses Turing AI chip — same proprietary silicon as XPeng's vehicles. Cat-like spine articulation for flexibility. Demonstrated walking through factory at XPeng's Tech Day Nov 2024. Mass production targeted 2026.

name: K2
desc: Kepler Robotics' K2 — second-generation industrial humanoid. Linear actuators + harmonic drive joints, anthropomorphic dexterous hand (11 DOF), 15kg payload. Targeted at automotive, logistics, security patrol.

name: 4NE-1
desc: NEURA Robotics flagship humanoid — German cognitive robotics with AI-native design. Integrates with NEURA's Neuraverse cognitive OS. 4NE-1 means '4th Neuraverse Edition 1'. 20kg payload, multi-domain perception, force-aware manipulation. Used in pharma, electronics, hospitality.

name: MiPa Gen 3
desc: NEURA Robotics MiPa Gen 3 — third-generation cognitive service robot. Wheeled humanoid platform for hospitality and reception, integrated with Neuraverse cognitive OS.

name: Sophia
desc: Hanson Robotics' famous social humanoid. First robot granted citizenship (Saudi Arabia, 2017). Designed by David Hanson with patented Frubber skin for realistic facial expressions. 60+ facial expressions, gaze tracking, conversational AI. Public-facing celebrity robot — appeared at UN, talk shows, conferences worldwide. Primarily an AI conversation platform; locomotion is limited.

name: TIAGo
desc: PAL Robotics TIAGo — single-arm wheeled humanoid, widely deployed in academic research. ROS-native, modular (different head/arm/hand configurations). 100+ universities deployed worldwide.

name: TALOS
desc: PAL Robotics TALOS — full-size 175cm bipedal humanoid for industrial research. Custom electric actuators in all 32 joints. Torque-controlled, ROS 2 compatible. Used by aerospace + automotive research labs.

name: CyberOne
desc: Xiaomi's first humanoid robot, unveiled August 2022 by Lei Jun. 21 joints, 30 kg payload-grade actuators (peak torque 300 N·m). Mi-AI environment perception, OAK depth vision, MiAI semantic recognition. Emotion recognition (85 environmental sounds, 45 human emotions). Mostly demonstration platform — limited commercial deployment.

name: STAR1
desc: RobotEra (Tsinghua University spin-off) STAR1 — set world record running humanoid speed at 3.6 m/s. 55 DOF, lightweight design with high-torque joints. Research and demo platform.

name: L7
desc: RobotEra second-generation humanoid for industrial deployment. Improved torque density, longer endurance than STAR1.

name: S1
desc: Astribot's S1 — wheeled humanoid with extremely fast arms. Demonstrated chopping vegetables, pouring drinks, folding shirts. 1m/s arm tip speed, 10kg arm payload. Wheel-based mobility rather than legs.

name: EM02
desc: EngineAI EM02 — bipedal humanoid focused on natural walking gait. Open-source SDK for research community.

name: DR01
desc: Industrial quadruped from DEEP Robotics, the Chinese quadruped specialist (also makers of Jueying X20/X30 series). Targets industrial inspection and outdoor patrol use cases.

name: N1
desc: Noetix N1 — research humanoid focused on dynamic locomotion. Demonstrated parkour-style movement in early footage.

name: Promobot V4
desc: Russian/Cypriot service humanoid for retail and reception. 100,000-word conversation vocabulary, facial recognition, wheel-based mobility. Deployed in shopping malls, banks, hotels.

name: Sprout
desc: Fauna Robotics' Sprout — service-focused humanoid in development. US startup.

name: T-HR3
desc: Toyota's third-generation Humanoid Robot — teleoperated avatar designed for remote presence and high-precision manipulation. Operator wore haptic exoskeleton + HMD for full-body remote control. 29 DOF, torque servo modules in all joints for safe human-environment interaction. Historic teleoperation milestone.

name: ASIMO
desc: Honda's iconic Advanced Step in Innovative MObility. THE humanoid robot of the 2000s — defined what humanoid robotics could look like for the public. Walked, ran, climbed stairs, served drinks, conducted orchestras. Final generation (2011) ran at 9 km/h, jumped, hopped on one leg. Honda retired ASIMO in March 2018 after 18 years of development. Historic — predates current humanoid wave by decades.

name: Pepper
desc: SoftBank/Aldebaran's social humanoid — over 30,000 units deployed worldwide in retail, banking, hospitality, education. Tablet-mounted interface, emotion recognition, multilingual conversation. SoftBank halted production June 2021. Aldebaran (the actual designer) entered bankruptcy in February 2025. Pepper marked the first mass-deployed social humanoid.

name: NAO
desc: Aldebaran's iconic NAO — the most-deployed humanoid in academia ever. Over 13,000 units sold across 70+ countries by 2018. RoboCup standard platform for over a decade. 6th generation (NAO 6, 2018) was the final version. SoftBank/Aldebaran entered bankruptcy February 2025; NAO production ceased.

name: Delivery Robot Gen 5
desc: Original 6-wheel sidewalk delivery robot. Active on 50+ university campuses globally. 11M+ delivery miles logged.

name: Delivery Robot Gen 6
desc: Gen 6 with improved sensors, AI, weather handling. €83.6M funding round 2024. RaaS model.

name: R1
desc: Nuro's first road-going autonomous delivery vehicle. Pioneered driverless grocery delivery. Kroger pilot.

name: R2
desc: Production Nuro R2 — first NHTSA-exempted autonomous delivery vehicle. Domino's pizza, Walmart, FedEx pilots.

name: R3
desc: 3rd-gen Nuro with BYD partnership for manufacturing. 10-year Uber Eats deal. Built for commercial scale.

name: Serve Gen 1
desc: Postmates spinoff. 4-wheel sidewalk delivery. Pink color signature. Uber Eats partner since 2022.

name: Serve Gen 2
desc: Gen 2 with NVIDIA Jetson Orin. Level 4 autonomy in defined areas. Major Uber Eats LA expansion.

name: Serve Gen 3
desc: 2025 Gen 3 — targeting 2,000-unit fleet rollout. Improved range, payload, weather handling. NVIDIA-powered.

name: Kiwibot 5.0
desc: 5th-gen with focus on Level 4 autonomy. UBC Vancouver launch 2025. Pittsburgh, Miami, LA cities.

name: Model C
desc: Vision-only sidewalk delivery (no LiDAR). Ex-Google engineers founded. Mitsubishi partnership for Japan deployment.

name: Courier
desc: Campus version of Cartken's sidewalk bot. Grubhub partnership at OSU + other universities.

name: Coco 2
desc: Gen 2 with more autonomy. OpenAI partnership for AI navigation. Multi-city expansion.

name: REV-1
desc: Three-wheel delivery robot that uses BIKE LANES, not sidewalks. Weather-tolerant. Originally Ann Arbor / Austin.

name: Tinymile
desc: Miami sidewalk delivery robot. Teleoperated last-mile food delivery.

name: Tortoise
desc: Walmart-tested sidewalk delivery robot. Teleoperated model. Compact form factor.

name: Avride Robotaxi
desc: Yandex spinoff. Robotaxi in Dallas via Uber partnership. Ex-Yandex self-driving team.

name: Clevon 1
desc: Estonian autonomous road-going delivery vehicle. European focus. Self-driving last-mile.

name: Meituan RB1
desc: Meituan's sidewalk delivery robot. Commercial operations in Shenzhen, Beijing for food delivery.

name: JD X
desc: JD.com's autonomous delivery vehicle. Multi-compartment for multiple parcels. Operating in Chinese cities.

name: Cainiao Xiaomanlv
desc: Alibaba Cainiao's sidewalk delivery robot. 'Little Donkey' model. High-volume Chinese e-commerce delivery.

name: BellaBot
desc: Cat-faced food delivery robot — viral hit in restaurants. 4-tray design. Touch-responsive cat face.

name: BellaBot Pro
desc: BellaBot Pro — 10.1" interactive touchscreen. Advanced navigation. Hospitality, retail.

name: KettyBot
desc: Compact 55cm-narrow delivery robot for tight spaces. Built-in advertising screen. Small restaurant favorite.

name: KettyBot Pro
desc: KettyBot Pro — 18.5" display, 3-in-1 (delivery, reception, marketing). 9-hour runtime. Smart tray detection.

name: PuduBot 2
desc: Heavy-duty delivery robot. 66kg payload. 7-tray capacity. Industrial-grade frame for buffets, hospital catering.

name: PuduBot 3
desc: 3rd-gen heavy-duty delivery. Improved sensors and AI. Industrial logistics, large-venue F&B.

name: CC1
desc: Hybrid cleaning + delivery robot. Scrubbing, sweeping, disinfecting in one. Multi-function commercial.

name: DinerBot T1
desc: KEENON's first delivery robot from 2016. Pioneer of indoor restaurant delivery. Now retired.

name: DinerBot T8
desc: Mid-range 4-tray restaurant delivery robot. Reliable workhorse for mid-sized restaurants.

name: DinerBot T9
desc: Premium service robot. 11.6" touchscreen. LiDAR + Visual SLAM. Auto-charging dock. Multi-mode.

name: DinerBot T9 Pro
desc: Upgraded T9 Pro — 15-hour runtime, die-cast chassis. Faster, more durable. 70cm minimum passage.

name: DinerBot T10
desc: Flagship T10 with movable head, 23.8" display, AI tray detection, 360° obstacle avoidance with stereo vision + VSLAM.

name: DinerBot T11
desc: 2025 T11 — newest flagship. Improved AI, larger screen, enhanced delivery scheduling.

name: ButlerBot W3
desc: Hotel room service delivery. Multi-floor with elevator integration. Hygienic compartmentalized handling.

name: S100
desc: 100kg+ payload heavy-load robot. Three charging methods incl. quick-swap battery. 360° obstacle avoidance. Industrial logistics.

name: Carti
desc: Heavy-duty Carti for retail/warehousing logistics. 2024 launch. Multi-bin delivery.

name: Relay
desc: Originally Savioke. Hotel room service delivery robot. Aloft Hotels deployment (Marriott).

name: Relay Plus
desc: Upgraded Relay with larger payload and improved navigation. Multi-floor hotel use.

name: Yeti 2.0
desc: Yeti 2.0 — improved Ottonomy delivery bot. Indoor + outdoor. Cincinnati airport ongoing deployment.

name: RoboCoffee
desc: OrionStar's coffee-making + delivery robot. Mall/airport beverage kiosks.

name: Lucki Pro
desc: OrionStar's restaurant delivery robot. Budget-friendly alternative to BellaBot/T8.

name: Flash
desc: Affordable Chinese delivery robot for restaurants. Entry-level alternative.

name: RoboShuttle
desc: YOGO's RoboShuttle for office building deliveries. Multi-floor elevator integration.

name: Relay Pharmaceutical
desc: Hospital pharmaceutical delivery robot. Medication transport. Healthcare-grade compliance.

name: Moxi
desc: Hospital nursing assistant + delivery robot. Social arm for non-clinical tasks. Frees nurses for patient care.

name: Vector
desc: Warehouse picking-assist delivery robot. Used in major fulfillment centers. RaaS pricing.

name: Chuck
desc: Warehouse picking robot. Shopify-acquired (now sold to Ocado). Workhorse for fulfillment.

name: Freight500
desc: Warehouse AMR for case/pallet moving. Zebra Technologies acquired. Industrial use.

name: UDA
desc: Chinese autonomous road delivery vehicle. Commercial operations in Shenzhen.

name: DroneSentry
desc: Docked autonomous patrol + light delivery for industrial/critical infrastructure security.

name: Mini 2
desc: Sub-250g foldable beginner drone with 4K/30p video and 10km transmission. Legacy popular entry-level option.

name: Mini 4K
desc: Sub-$300 entry-level 4K drone. Sub-250g. Best budget beginner option in 2026.

name: Mini 5 Pro
desc: 2025 flagship sub-250g with 1-inch sensor (industry first at this weight). Omnidirectional sensing. 4K HDR.

name: Air 3S
desc: Dual-camera (50MP wide 1-inch + 48MP tele). LiDAR for low-light obstacle sensing. ActiveTrack 360. Best enthusiast pick 2026.

name: Mavic 4 Pro
desc: 2025 flagship — 100MP Hasselblad camera + tele cameras. 6K video. Best camera drone overall 2026.

name: Avata
desc: Compact cinewhoop-style FPV drone for indoor + agile flying. Accessible FPV with motion controller.

name: Avata 360
desc: 2026 360-camera FPV drone — likely DJI/Insta360 collaboration. Reframe shots in post.

name: FPV
desc: Original DJI FPV drone — fast (up to 140 km/h) racing-style with goggles. Pro pilots.

name: Neo
desc: Compact selfie-drone with palm launch + AI tracking. Sub-250g. Safe frame. Most affordable DJI drone.

name: Flip
desc: 2025 Flip — unique folding selfie-style drone. AI follows + obstacle avoidance.

name: Lito X1
desc: April 2026 launch — DJI's new entry-level Lito series. Below Flip in tier. Ultra-portable beginner drone.

name: Inspire 3
desc: Pro cinema flagship — full-frame 8K Zenmuse X9-8K Air. Apple ProRes. RTK. Used in major Hollywood productions.

name: Inspire 2
desc: Predecessor pro cinema drone with swappable Zenmuse cameras. Workhorse for indie/commercial productions.

name: Phantom 4 Pro V2.0
desc: Legacy Phantom prosumer drone with 1-inch CMOS. Popular for mapping/surveying. Last of the Phantom line.

name: Matrice 350 RTK
desc: Mid-size enterprise drone with RTK + modular payloads (Zenmuse H20T/H30T/L2 LiDAR/P1). Industry inspection.

name: Matrice 400
desc: 2025 flagship enterprise — replaces M300/M350. Improved payload capacity, longer flight, better RTK.

name: Agras T40
desc: 40kg spraying capacity agricultural drone. Coaxial rotor design. RTK + omnidirectional radar.

name: Agras T50
desc: 75kg payload spraying + spreading drone. RTK. Best-selling pro agriculture drone.

name: Agras T100
desc: 2025 100kg payload flagship agricultural drone. Tank-grade for large-scale farming.

name: EVO II Pro V3
desc: V3 with 1-inch CMOS, 6K HDR, Moonlight 2.0 low-light. 40-minute flight. SkyLink 2.0 15km.

name: EVO II Pro RTK
desc: RTK version for cm-accurate mapping/surveying. 1-inch CMOS. 40-min flight.

name: EVO II Dual 640T V3
desc: Radiometric thermal (640x512) + 8K visual cameras. Public safety, inspection, search/rescue.

name: EVO II Enterprise V3
desc: Enterprise version with modular accessories. 8K visual. RTK optional. Spotlight + speaker.

name: Raptor T
desc: NDAA-compliant enterprise drone based on Mavic 3 Enterprise platform. Made in USA. Government-eligible.

name: Raptor
desc: NDAA-compliant Raptor (non-thermal) for government mapping. Mavic 3 Enterprise platform.

name: X10
desc: Enterprise AI-pilot drone for public safety, defense. NDAA-compliant. Best-in-class autonomy.

name: X10D
desc: Military variant of X10 for defense. Blue sUAS-cleared. ISR missions. US Army programs.

name: RCR
desc: Remote Control Drone — docked station + autonomous patrols. Persistent monitoring for utilities/infrastructure.

name: LEMUR-S
desc: Tactical indoor drone for police. Glass breaker, two-way audio, self-righting, drop-resistant.

name: LEMUR 2
desc: Upgraded LEMUR 2 — improved sensors, real-time floor plans, mesh networking. Police/tactical use.

name: Responder
desc: Drone-as-First-Responder system. Docked at fire/police stations, launched on 911 dispatch.

name: Guardian
desc: 2026 flagship — Starlink-connected drone designed to replace police helicopters. 75-inch wingspan, 48.6 lb max takeoff.

name: Ghost X
desc: Military VTOL ISR drone with Lattice AI for autonomous mission execution. Multi-vehicle teaming.

name: Altius 700M
desc: Tube-launched loitering munition for military. ISR + strike capability. 75-min loiter.

name: Bolt
desc: Backpack-portable autonomous military drone. ISR + light strike capability.

name: Platform 1
desc: Original fixed-wing medical delivery drone. Parachute-drop to recipient. Rwanda/Ghana medical supply pioneer.

name: Platform 2
desc: 2024 last-mile delivery drone. Quiet operation. Lowers droid on tether for precision placement.

name: Hummingbird
desc: Alphabet's delivery drone. Hybrid VTOL. Operating in US, Australia, Finland for last-mile delivery.

name: M2
desc: Medical/logistics delivery drone. Used by UPS, NHS for blood/sample transport.

name: MK30
desc: Amazon's latest Prime Air delivery drone. Launched commercially 2024 in US. Quieter, longer-range than predecessors.

name: Teal 2
desc: Blue sUAS-cleared military/government drone. SRR (Short Range Reconnaissance). Thermal optional.

name: Black Widow
desc: 2025 Black Widow — Army SRR Tranche 2 selection. Improved range, payload, autonomy.

name: Trinity Pro
desc: VTOL fixed-wing surveying drone. 90-min endurance. RTK + PPK. German-made for industrial mapping.

name: Vector
desc: Military VTOL ISR drone — heavily used in Ukraine. Long endurance reconnaissance.

name: WingtraOne Gen II
desc: VTOL fixed-wing surveying drone. 59-min flight. PPK accurate. Swiss-engineered for surveying.

name: Commander 3 XL
desc: NDAA-compliant public safety/military drone. 3-hour swap. Made in Canada/USA.

name: Typhoon H Plus
desc: Hexacopter consumer drone with Intel RealSense. Legacy popular American-brand option.

name: H850 RTK
desc: Enterprise hexacopter with RTK for mapping/surveying. 55-min flight.

name: HS720E
desc: Affordable beginner brushless GPS drone. 4K UHD. Common entry point under $300.

name: HS900
desc: Mid-range Holy Stone with obstacle sensing. 4K HDR. Best budget option in 2024-2026.

name: Tello
desc: Programmable beginner/education drone. Scratch + Python coding. DJI-powered camera. Massive education adoption.

name: Tello EDU
desc: Education version of Tello with swarm flight + mission pads. STEM curriculum staple.

name: Zino Mini Pro
desc: Sub-250g budget alternative to DJI Mini. Three-way obstacle sensing. 4K HDR.

name: Aibao FPV
desc: FPV racing-style drone for beginners. Walkera legacy brand from China.

name: Antigravity A1
desc: Insta360's first drone — 360° camera with reframe-in-post. Competes with DJI Avata 360.

name: X1
desc: Pocket-sized selfie drone with prop-guards. AI subject tracking. Massive online success.

name: X1 Pro
desc: Upgraded X1 Pro — 8K video, longer battery, improved tracking. 2025 launch.

name: Atom 2
desc: Budget sub-250g 4K beginner drone. Solid Mini 3 alternative under $400.

name: SOTEN
desc: NDAA-compliant Japanese enterprise drone. Blue UAS approved. Made in Japan for govt/inspection.

name: PowerEgg X
desc: Convertible drone — flies as drone, lands on water, or works as handheld AI camera. Unique form factor.

name: Tango2
desc: NDAA-compliant compact public safety drone. Made in Canada. Police/EMS focus.

name: Edge 130
desc: NDAA-compliant compact military drone. Red Cat/Teal parent company. Blue UAS approved.

name: Puma 3 AE
desc: Hand-launched fixed-wing ISR drone. US DoD standard. 2.5-hour endurance.

name: Switchblade 300
desc: Tube-launched loitering munition. Backpack-portable. Widely deployed in US military operations.

name: V-BAT
desc: VTOL military drone with Hivemind AI for autonomous swarm operations. DoD deployments.

name: Elios 3
desc: Caged indoor inspection drone with LiDAR for confined spaces (sewers, tanks, mines). Swiss-engineered.

name: Aero
desc: Level 4 autonomy indoor drone for mining/inspection. Penn-spinout. LiDAR SLAM in GPS-denied environments.

name: Flytrex Drone
desc: Israeli last-mile delivery drone. Operates in US (NC, TX). Cable-lowered package drop.

name: EH216-S
desc: World's first commercially certified autonomous passenger eVTOL. China-certified for commercial passenger service.

name: Waymo Driver (Jaguar I-PACE)
desc: Waymo's Level 4 robotaxi platform on Jaguar I-PACE. 2,000+ vehicles, 250,000+ weekly paid rides across SF/Phoenix/LA. Alphabet-backed.

name: Zeekr RT
desc: Purpose-built Waymo robotaxi by Zeekr (Geely). Replacing I-PACE fleet. 6-seat, longer range, no steering wheel. Phoenix launch 2025.

name: Cybercab
desc: Purpose-built Tesla robotaxi. No steering wheel. 2-seat design. Production starting 2026 Fremont. Target $30K consumer price.

name: Zoox Robotaxi
desc: Amazon-owned. Purpose-built bidirectional robotaxi — no front or back. Symmetric sensor suite. SF + Las Vegas Strip + airport. Austin/Miami coming.

name: Apollo Go RT5
desc: Baidu's commercial robotaxi. 17M+ rides completed, 240M+ km driven. Operating in Wuhan, Beijing, Shenzhen. Dubai expansion 2026.

name: Apollo Go RT6
desc: 6th-gen purpose-built robotaxi. 60% cost reduction. No steering wheel option. Production at scale starting 2024.

name: Robotaxi GXR
desc: WeRide's robotaxi. 1,600+ vehicle fleet globally. Abu Dhabi, Dubai, Singapore, France, Belgium operations. Uber partner.

name: Robobus
desc: Autonomous Level 4 shuttle bus. Belgium's first federal L4 permit. Runs between Leuven station and corridor with safety officer.

name: PonyTaxi Gen 7
desc: Pony.ai's 7th-gen robotaxi. 1,400+ fleet. Beijing, Shenzhen, Guangzhou + Dubai 2026 launch. Uber + Stellantis Europe partners.

name: DiDi RoboRide
desc: DiDi's autonomous ride-hailing service. Shanghai operations. Integrated into DiDi app for hybrid human/robot fleet.

name: IV.5 Robotaxi
desc: SAIC's autonomous taxi platform. Shanghai commercial operations.

name: Ioniq 5 Robotaxi
desc: Hyundai-Aptiv joint venture robotaxi on Ioniq 5. Las Vegas, LA service via Uber and Lyft.

name: Wayve Driver
desc: AI-first self-driving platform — end-to-end ML, no HD maps. London testing. Uber partnership. Lyft UK/Germany 2026.

name: Momenta MSD
desc: Chinese AI self-driving platform. Licensed to Mercedes, Stellantis, Toyota, GM. Robotaxi pilots.

name: Verne 2-Seater Robotaxi
desc: Rimac-backed European robotaxi. Purpose-built 2-seat design. Zagreb launch 2026. Croatia/Europe focus.

name: May Mobility Shuttle
desc: Public transit autonomous shuttle. Level 4. Operating in 7+ US cities for fixed-route transit. Toyota partnership.

name: Beep Shuttle
desc: Autonomous shuttle operator. Operates Yutong/EZ10 shuttles for cities. Jacksonville and other Florida deployments.

name: Aurora Driver
desc: Level 4 autonomous trucking platform. Commercial launch April 2024. Peterbilt + Volvo Trucks integration. Texas highways.

name: Kodiak Driver
desc: First US driverless commercial trucks (Dec 2024). 10 driverless trucks. 5,200+ paid hours. 3M+ autonomous miles. Dallas-Houston public road operations.

name: Waabi Driver
desc: AI-first autonomous truck. Simulation-heavy training. Texas commercial launch 2025. Uber Freight partnership.

name: PlusCore
desc: L4 trucking platform. Software-first. International Trucks integration. PlusDrive ADAS-as-stepping-stone strategy.

name: Gatik Class 6/7
desc: Middle-mile autonomous trucking. Walmart Bentonville driverless since 2021. Class 6/7 box trucks. Loblaw Canada partnership.

name: Torc Daimler Truck
desc: Daimler-owned autonomous trucking subsidiary. Freightliner Cascadia integration. Schneider, CR England partnerships.

name: Einride Pod
desc: Cabless all-electric autonomous truck. Swedish-engineered. GE Appliances commercial deployment. US public road testing.

name: Stack AV Class 8
desc: Ex-Argo AI team. SoftBank-backed. Pittsburgh-based autonomous trucking. 2024 commercial launch.

name: Xuanyuan
desc: Chinese autonomous trucking leader. Delivered 400 autonomous heavy trucks to ZTO Express. Large-scale commercial.

name: Yardbot
desc: Autonomous yard truck for warehouse/distribution centers. Short-haul logistics. RaaS pricing. Schneider partner.

name: AIMD
desc: Military-grade autonomous ground vehicle platform. NDAA-compliant. US DoD pilots.

name: EpicSim
desc: Simulation + testing software for AV/AD developers. Used by Ford, Toyota, Audi, Porsche. Industry-standard validation tool.

name: AT128 LiDAR
desc: Hesai's automotive LiDAR — cost-leader for L2+ ADAS and robotaxi. Industry shipment leader.

name: Iris LiDAR
desc: Long-range 1550nm LiDAR. Volvo EX90 + Polestar 3 production. Mercedes partnership.

name: EyeQ6
desc: 6th-gen Mobileye chip for ADAS/AD. Intel-spinout. 800+ vehicle models use Mobileye. Industry leader in driver-assist.

name: STORMRUNNER
desc: Autonomous marine vessel for defense. Leonardo DRS partnership for aerial threat neutralization. Mobile defense platform.

name: R2 Robotaxi
desc: Uber's $1.25B commitment for 50,000 R2-based robotaxis across 25 cities. Level 4 in-house. Custom 5nm chip + LiDAR.

name: Lucid Midsize Robotaxi
desc: Uber + Lucid robotaxi partnership. 20,000 units initially, potentially doubling. Luxury robotaxi tier.

name: BlueROV2
desc: Most popular sub-$10K ROV. Open-source. 6 or 8 thrusters. Raspberry Pi-based. 100m depth (300m extended).

name: BlueROV3
desc: Next-gen BlueROV with Navigator flight controller, BlueOS. Improved sensors, better autonomy. 2024 launch.

name: Seaeye Falcon
desc: World's most popular professional portable electric ROV. UCO has 33-unit fleet. Offshore wind, defense, oil/gas.

name: Seaeye Lynx
desc: Deep-water electric ROV (1500m). Used to survey 18th-century galleon San José.

name: Seaeye Sabertooth
desc: Hybrid AUV/ROV. 360° hovering. Single hull (1200m) or double (3000m). Autonomous inspection + maintenance.

name: eWROV
desc: Full-size electric work-class ROV equivalent to 250HP hydraulic. Ocean Infinity launch customer. Offshore energy.

name: Dive-LD
desc: Large-displacement AUV for military undersea ISR. Long endurance. US Navy programs.

name: Dive-XL
desc: Extra-large AUV — underwater mothership. Launches Copperhead AUVs + Seabed Sentry. US Navy CAMP project.

name: Copperhead
desc: Small launched-from-Dive-XL AUV. Torpedo-style. Multi-mission.

name: Seabed Sentry
desc: Seabed-residency monitoring AUV. Persistent undersea surveillance. Launches from Dive-XL.

name: Blue Whale (Kraken)
desc: Anduril/Kraken partnership. Long-range high-performance USV. Modular payloads. US Navy hybrid fleet.

name: Boxfish AUV
desc: Tetherless hovering AUV. 6 degrees of freedom. NZ-engineered. Marine science + environmental monitoring.

name: Luna ROV
desc: Live underwater exploration ROV. Real-time observation. Designed for live-streamed scientific exploration.

name: MOLA AUV
desc: Portable research AUV. Deployed under 2m Arctic sea ice for high-res mapping. MBARI CoMPAS Lab.

name: Iver4
desc: Compact portable AUV. US Navy hydrographic surveys. Commercial bathymetric mapping.

name: Gavia
desc: Modular AUV for oceanographic surveys. Customizable sensor payload. Sub-100kg.

name: Slocum Glider
desc: Underwater glider. Buoyancy-driven (no propeller). Up to 12-month endurance. Ocean climate research.

name: Wave Glider
desc: Wave-powered surface glider. Boeing subsidiary. Persistent ocean monitoring. Months at sea.

name: HUGIN Superior
desc: Premier commercial AUV for oil/gas, hydrography. Up to 6,000m depth. Norwegian-engineered.

name: REMUS 100
desc: Navy standard AUV. Mine countermeasures, hydrographic surveys. 100m depth. Man-portable.

name: REMUS 6000
desc: Famous deep AUV — found Air France 447 wreckage, surveyed Titanic. 6,000m depth.

name: Revolution
desc: Compact battery-internal ROV. 305m depth. Inspection-grade. No surface tether needed for power.

name: FIFISH V6 Expert
desc: Consumer/prosumer ROV. 4K/100p camera. 100m depth. Most popular underwater drone for filmmakers.

name: FIFISH W6
desc: Industrial work-class with robotic arm. 350m depth. Inspection, light intervention.

name: M2 Pro
desc: Consumer ROV. 150m depth. 4K camera. Affordable underwater drone.

name: M2 S
desc: Upgraded M2 with optional robotic arm. 100m depth. Hobbyist-prosumer bridge.

name: Trident
desc: Open-source underwater drone. WiFi-tethered. Education + citizen science. Sofar Ocean acquisition.

name: SwarmDiver
desc: Swarming AUV — multiple units coordinate. Navy ISR, surveillance. Multi-vehicle autonomy.

name: 510 PackBot
desc: Most-deployed EOD robot worldwide. 4,500+ in service. Used at 9/11, Iraq, Afghanistan, Fukushima nuclear cleanup, Boston Marathon bombing.

name: Andros F6B
desc: Used by 90% of US bomb squads. Stair-climbing, multi-tool. Industry standard for police EOD.

name: Titus
desc: Backpackable compact EOD robot. Tactical police use. Faster deployment than Andros.

name: CALIBER MK3
desc: Canadian-made EOD robot. Modular design. Used by police agencies worldwide.

name: Bobcat
desc: French-made EOD robot. European military + police use. Versatile modular platform.

name: Quince
desc: Famous Fukushima robot. Mapped radiation distribution across multiple floors after PackBot. Japanese USAR pioneer.

name: Spirit
desc: Compact urban search & rescue robot. DARPA research lineage. Now part of Blue Origin.

name: WALK-MAN
desc: Italian disaster response humanoid. 1.85m, 102kg, 33 DoF. DARPA Robotics Challenge derived research.

name: Centauro
desc: Hybrid wheel-legged centaur design. 1.5m, 93kg. 4 legs with wheels for tough terrain disaster response.

name: Thermite RS1
desc: Heavy-duty firefighting robot with water cannon (1,250 GPM). Used at LA, NY, structural firefighting. Crew protection.

name: Thermite RS3
desc: Larger Thermite RS3. 2-axis water/foam cannon. FDNY purchase. Industrial + structural firefighting.

name: Colossus
desc: FAMOUS — saved Notre-Dame Cathedral during 2019 fire. French-made firefighting robot. Heavy-water-cannon delivery.

name: LUF 60
desc: Austrian firefighting robot. Specialized for tunnel/underground fires. High-pressure water-fog attack.

name: 110 FirstLook
desc: Throwable tactical reconnaissance robot. Survives 15-ft drops. Police SWAT + military. Real-time video.

name: Throwbot 2
desc: Ultra-compact throwable robot. <2 lb. IR + visual camera. Police/military reconnaissance.

name: teleMAX EVO
desc: German EOD robot. Modular design. 7-DOF arm. European police/military standard.

name: T-TR1
desc: Toyota's telepresence disaster response platform. Japanese rescue tech.

name: Aerial Fire Rescue
desc: Aerial wildfire inspection drone. Thermal mapping for active fire perimeters.

name: Aerial Firefighter Drone
desc: Aerial fire intelligence + tanker coordination drones. Wildfire management.

name: MTRS Mk II
desc: Medium-sized tactical robot (MTRS). US Army field deployment. Multi-mission EOD.

name: 310 SUGV
desc: Small UGV. Army standard for tactical recon/EOD. Backpackable.

name: Spot (Firefighter Configuration)
desc: Specialized Spot configuration for fire department deployments. Adds thermal imaging payload, hazmat-resistant pads, and emergency response software. Used by NYPD, LAFD, Tokyo FD and other emergency services for hazardous-area reconnaissance and victim search in unsafe structures.

name: S5 Patrol
desc: Autonomous outdoor security patrol robot. Alarm response. 24/7 perimeter security.

name: Mini-CALIBER
desc: Compact CALIBER variant. Sub-50lb. Police rapid-response EOD.

name: Rhyno Protect
desc: French crowd management / civil protection robot. Police deployment. Civil disturbance response.

name: RapidBridge
desc: DARPA project — rapid bridge deployment for disaster recovery. Engineering robot for cut-off areas.

name: Sojourner
desc: First successful Mars rover. Operated for 83 days as part of the Mars Pathfinder mission. Microwave-sized, solar-powered, traveled approximately 100 meters total.

name: Spirit (MER-A)
desc: Mars Exploration Rover A. Operated for 6 years (planned: 90 days). Discovered evidence of past water at Gusev Crater. Got stuck in soft soil in 2009, last communication 2010.

name: Opportunity (MER-B)
desc: Mars Exploration Rover B. Operated for nearly 15 years (planned: 90 days). Traveled 45 km on Mars. Lost in 2018 global dust storm. 'My battery is low and it's getting dark' became iconic farewell.

name: Curiosity
desc: Mars Science Laboratory rover. Car-sized, RTG-powered (no solar limit). Has been exploring Gale Crater since 2012. ChemCam laser spectrometer. Confirmed Mars once had habitable conditions.

name: Perseverance
desc: NASA's flagship Mars rover. Caching samples for future Mars Sample Return mission. Carries MOXIE (produced oxygen from CO2). Deployed Ingenuity helicopter. Jezero Crater (ancient lake delta).

name: Ingenuity
desc: First powered flight on another planet (April 19, 2021). Originally planned for 5 flights, completed 72. Ended mission January 2024 after rotor damage. Carried piece of Wright Flyer fabric.

name: Lunokhod 1
desc: First successful Moon rover. Soviet program. Operated November 1970 - September 1971 in Mare Imbrium. Traveled 10.5 km over 11 lunar days. Bath-tub shape on 8 wheels.

name: Lunokhod 2
desc: Second Soviet Moon rover. Set distance record until 2014 (broken by Opportunity on Mars). Traveled 39 km in 4 months. Le Monnier crater.

name: Yutu
desc: China's first Moon rover. Part of Chang'e 3 mission. Operated 31 months (planned 3 months). Mobility issues from Jan 2014 but kept transmitting science data.

name: Yutu-2
desc: First rover on the far side of the Moon. Chang'e 4 mission. Active since January 2019. Operates in Von Kármán crater. Communicates via Queqiao relay satellite.

name: Pragyan
desc: India's first Moon rover. Chandrayaan-3 mission. First mission to land near the lunar south pole (August 2023). Operated one lunar day (~14 Earth days) before lunar night.

name: Zhurong
desc: China's first Mars rover. Tianwen-1 mission. Landed Utopia Planitia May 2021. Operated 358 sols (planned 90). Went into hibernation May 2022, never reactivated.

name: SLIM
desc: Smart Lander for Investigating Moon ('Moon Sniper'). First pinpoint lunar landing (55m from target, target was within 100m). Landed January 19, 2024 on Shioli crater slope. Solar issue limited operations. Deployed LEV-1 + LEV-2 rovers. Operations terminated August 2024.

name: LEV-1
desc: Lunar Excursion Vehicle 1. Hopping rover deployed by SLIM January 2024. Smallest/lightest case of direct lunar-to-Earth data transmission (380,000 km). Performed autonomous hopping locomotion. Standby on lunar surface.

name: LEV-2 (SORA-Q)
desc: Smallest and lightest lunar rover ever. Baseball-sized transformable sphere. Co-developed with Tomy (toys), Sony, Doshisha University. Drove on Moon, imaged SLIM. Frog/turtle-inspired locomotion.

name: Viking 1 Lander
desc: First spacecraft to successfully soft-land on Mars and complete its mission. Equipped with a robotic surface sampler arm that scooped Martian soil into onboard biology, chemistry, and meteorology instruments. Operated for over 6 years on the surface.

name: Viking 2 Lander
desc: Second Viking lander, touched down at Utopia Planitia in September 1976. Identical hardware to Viking 1 with a robotic surface sampler arm. Operated for nearly 4 years before battery failure.

name: Phoenix
desc: Polar Mars lander equipped with a 2.35 m robotic arm capable of digging trenches to access subsurface water ice. Confirmed the presence of water ice on Mars and operated for 5 months before the Martian winter ended its mission.

name: InSight
desc: Interior Exploration using Seismic Investigations, Geodesy and Heat Transport. Mars lander equipped with a robotic instrument deployment arm that placed a seismometer and a self-hammering heat probe (HP3 'mole') on the surface. Detected over 1,300 marsquakes before being decommissioned in late 2022.

name: Vikram
desc: Chandrayaan-3 lunar lander. Soft-landed near the lunar south pole in August 2023, making India the fourth nation to achieve a soft Moon landing and the first to land in the south polar region. Deployed the Pragyan rover.

name: Tianwen-1 Lander
desc: China's first Mars lander, part of the Tianwen-1 mission. Soft-landed at Utopia Planitia in May 2021 and deployed the Zhurong rover, making China the third nation to soft-land on Mars.

name: Huygens
desc: First and only spacecraft to land on a moon in the outer solar system. Released from the Cassini orbiter and parachuted to the surface of Saturn's moon Titan in January 2005, returning surface images and atmospheric data for 90 minutes after touchdown.

name: Philae
desc: First spacecraft to soft-land on a comet. Released by the Rosetta orbiter onto Comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko in November 2014. Bounced twice on landing and came to rest in a shadowed location, operating intermittently on battery power for 3 days before going silent.

name: Hayabusa
desc: World's first asteroid sample return mission. Rendezvoused with near-Earth asteroid 25143 Itokawa in 2005, performed touch-and-go sampling, and returned a small sample to Earth in 2010 despite numerous technical failures during the mission.

name: Hayabusa 2
desc: Successor to Hayabusa. Rendezvoused with asteroid 162173 Ryugu in 2018, deployed multiple landers (MINERVA-II rovers and MASCOT), created an artificial crater, and returned samples to Earth in December 2020. Now on an extended mission to asteroid 1998 KY26.

name: OSIRIS-REx / OSIRIS-APEX
desc: Origins, Spectral Interpretation, Resource Identification, and Security - Regolith Explorer. Collected samples from asteroid 101955 Bennu using its TAGSAM (Touch-and-Go Sample Acquisition Mechanism) arm and returned them to Earth in September 2023. Renamed OSIRIS-APEX for an extended mission to asteroid Apophis, arriving 2029.

name: Stardust
desc: First spacecraft to return samples from a comet. Flew through the coma of Comet Wild 2 in 2004, collecting particles in an aerogel collector, and returned the sample capsule to Earth in 2006. Later repurposed for a flyby of Comet Tempel 1 as Stardust-NExT.

name: MINERVA-II-1A (Rover 1A / HIBOU)
desc: Cylindrical hopping rover deployed by Hayabusa 2 onto asteroid Ryugu in September 2018. First robot to successfully operate on an asteroid surface, using internal torquers to hop in Ryugu's micro-gravity environment.

name: MINERVA-II-1B (Rover 1B / OWL)
desc: Companion hopping rover to MINERVA-II-1A. Deployed alongside its twin onto asteroid Ryugu by Hayabusa 2 in September 2018, returning surface imagery and temperature data from the asteroid surface.

name: MASCOT
desc: Mobile Asteroid Surface Scout. Shoebox-sized lander built by the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and France's CNES, deployed by Hayabusa 2 onto asteroid Ryugu in October 2018. Hopped once to reposition itself and operated for 17 hours on battery power.

name: Canadarm (SRMS)
desc: Shuttle Remote Manipulator System. 15.2 m, 6-DOF robotic arm operated on all 90 Space Shuttle missions from 1981 to 2011, deploying and retrieving payloads including the Hubble Space Telescope. Established Canadian leadership in space robotics.

name: Canadarm2 (SSRMS)
desc: Space Station Remote Manipulator System. 17.6 m, 7-DOF arm installed on the ISS in 2001. Capable of 'walking' along the station by attaching either end to a base point. Routinely captures visiting cargo spacecraft including SpaceX Dragon and Northrop Grumman Cygnus.

name: Dextre (SPDM)
desc: Special Purpose Dexterous Manipulator. Two-armed robot installed on the ISS in 2008, designed to perform precise maintenance tasks that previously required spacewalks. Attaches to the end of Canadarm2 or directly to the station structure.

name: JEMRMS
desc: Japanese Experiment Module Remote Manipulator System. Two-part robotic arm (main arm 10 m + small fine arm) attached to the Kibo module of the ISS. Handles external payloads on the Kibo Exposed Facility.

name: European Robotic Arm (ERA)
desc: 11.3 m symmetrical 7-DOF arm with end effectors at both ends, allowing it to 'walk' hand-over-hand around the Russian segment of the ISS. Launched on the Nauka module in July 2021 and operational since 2022 after a series of commissioning spacewalks.

name: Astrobee Honey
desc: One of three free-flying autonomous robots on the ISS. Cube-shaped robot uses electric fans for propulsion in microgravity, runs Android-based software, and serves as a platform for researchers to test guest-science payloads.

name: Astrobee Queen
desc: Second of three Astrobee free-flying robots on the ISS. Identical hardware to Honey and Bumble, used for autonomous navigation research, payload transport, and remote inspection inside the station.

name: Astrobee Bumble
desc: Third of three Astrobee free-flying robots on the ISS. Used for autonomous flight research, environmental monitoring, and supporting astronaut activities through teleoperation or scripted behaviors.

name: CIMON
desc: Crew Interactive Mobile Companion. Spherical AI assistant developed by Airbus and IBM (Watson) for DLR. Operated briefly on the ISS in 2018, designed to assist astronauts with experiments and provide voice-controlled information retrieval.

name: CIMON-2
desc: Second-generation Crew Interactive Mobile Companion. Improved AI emotional sensitivity, longer battery life, and more robust flight capability than CIMON. Operated on the ISS from 2019 with multiple successful astronaut interaction sessions.

name: Double 3
desc: The third-generation Double Robotics mobile telepresence robot. Introduced dual cameras with 13-megapixel stills and 150° wide-angle obstacle avoidance, plus a beamforming microphone array. Superseded by Double 4 in late 2024.

name: Double 4
desc: Fourth-generation flagship mobile telepresence robot from Double Robotics, unveiled November 2024. Improved obstacle avoidance, sturdier base for uneven floors, and seamless integration with Zoom, Microsoft Teams and Google Meet.
secondary_camera: Floor camera with HDR night vision

name: Double 2
desc: The robot that defined the consumer telepresence category. Self-balancing two-wheel base with iPad as the screen and brain, allowing remote workers to attend meetings, walk hallways, and tour facilities from anywhere.

name: BeamPro
desc: Enterprise telepresence robot that defined the high-end remote-presence category. Used widely in tech-company offices including by Edward Snowden remotely. Original Suitable Technologies wound down in 2020; brand revived with Beam Pro 3 in 2025.

name: Beam Pro 3
desc: Third-generation Beam Pro announced May 2025 as Suitable Technologies' return to the market. Features higher-resolution 4K video, improved battery life, and enhanced enterprise management tools.

name: Ohmni Supercam
desc: OhmniLabs' next-generation flagship launched March 2025, featuring ultra-high-resolution 4K camera and AI-powered auto-framing for healthcare, enterprise collaboration, and distance learning.

name: Ohmni
desc: OhmniLabs' original consumer-friendly mobile telepresence robot. Lightweight three-wheel design with HD video and tilt-screen mechanism for natural eye contact. Widely deployed in healthcare and remote-work contexts.

name: Temi
desc: Autonomous mobile robot blending telepresence with personal-assistant functionality. Uses 3D vision and LiDAR for autonomous navigation, can follow users, dock automatically, and deliver items between rooms.
languages_spoken: English, Mandarin, Hebrew, Spanish, French, German, Japanese, Arabic

name: Temi Pro
desc: Business-focused Temi launched July 2024 with enhanced autonomy, 4K camera, and improved navigation. Targeted at retail, healthcare, hospitality, and corporate deployments where reliability and fleet management matter.

name: Ava Telepresence
desc: Enterprise-grade autonomous telepresence robot built on Ava Robotics' navigation platform (spun out from iRobot). Self-navigates to meeting rooms, integrates with Cisco Webex and Microsoft Teams, and added AI environmental sensors via Cisco partnership in 2025.

name: VGo
desc: One of the earliest commercial telepresence robots. Widely deployed in K-12 schools to let homebound students attend classes, and in hospitals for remote patient consultations. Acquired by Vecna Technologies in 2015.

name: Anybots QB
desc: One of the first commercial telepresence robots. Self-balancing two-wheel design predated Double Robotics. Anybots discontinued the QB by 2014 before relaunching as Anybots 2.0 with industrial focus.

name: Anybots QX
desc: Industrial-focused telepresence robot completing beta testing in September 2024 with commercial launch Q2 2025. Ruggedized for remote industrial inspections in manufacturing and oil & gas, with thermal imaging and multi-terrain mobility.

name: Giraff
desc: Eldercare-focused telepresence robot for the European market. Used in numerous EU-funded research projects on independent living for older adults. Brand later transitioned to Camanio Care.

name: Teladoc InTouch Lite
desc: Clinical-grade telepresence robot for hospital deployments. Originally from InTouch Health (acquired by Teladoc in 2020 for $600M), used in stroke care, ICU consultations, and tele-ICU programs across major hospital networks worldwide.

name: Kubi
desc: Tabletop telepresence robot — a pan/tilt cradle for an iPad. Let remote participants look around a meeting room rather than being stuck with a fixed laptop view. Acquired by Xandex in 2017.

name: MantaroBot
desc: US-made mobile telepresence platform with customizable hardware configurations. Used by enterprise and government customers including military training and remote inspection applications.

name: PadBot U1
desc: Budget consumer mobile telepresence robot from Chinese manufacturer Inbot Technology. Mounted a tablet on a self-balancing base, targeting small-business and personal use cases at a fraction of premium-brand pricing.

name: Texai
desc: Research telepresence prototype from Willow Garage (also the birthplace of ROS and PR2). Internal deployment at Willow Garage allowed remote employees to be present in the office. Never sold commercially but influenced the entire category.

name: Cowboys Starbot
desc: Custom-branded Double Robotics telepresence robot deployed by the Dallas Cowboys in March 2022. Allows Cowboys athletes, cheerleaders and alumni to visit hospital patients digitally and safely. Notable example of telepresence branding for sports philanthropy.

name: PARO
desc: The original therapeutic social robot. Modeled on a baby harp seal, PARO is the longest-deployed eldercare robot worldwide with documented clinical benefits for dementia patients — reducing agitation and improving mood. FDA-cleared as a Class 2 medical device since 2009.

name: ElliQ 3
desc: Tabletop AI companion designed as a proactive engagement partner for older adults living alone. Deployed by New York State Office for the Aging and other US agency programs. Initiates conversations, sets medication reminders, leads cognitive exercises, and connects family via video call.
pilot_customers: NY State Office for the Aging

name: Moxie
desc: Companion robot for children ages 5-10 developed by Embodied (founded by former iRobot CTO Paolo Pirjanian). Used conversational AI and expressive animations to help kids develop emotional and social skills. Embodied wound down operations in late 2024 but units remain in active use.

name: Miko 3
desc: AI-powered conversational companion for children ages 5-10 combining play and STEM education. Indian unicorn valued at $550M with strong global sales. Includes built-in tablet face, voice interaction, and content library covering math, science, reading.

name: Miko Mini
desc: Compact, lower-cost sibling to Miko 3. Same conversational AI but in a static tabletop form. Targets gift-buyer parents at the sub-$150 price point and has been a strong holiday seller in US/UK markets.

name: Lovot
desc: Non-verbal emotional companion robot designed by ex-Pepper engineer Kaname Hayashi. Recognizes family members, responds to touch and voice, exhibits learned attachment behaviors. Wildly popular in Japan — sold tens of thousands of units despite the high price point.
shell_material: Soft fabric outer body, ABS frame

name: Jibo
desc: The world's first commercial social robot for the home. Developed by MIT Media Lab's Cynthia Breazeal. Sold from 2017-2018, NTT Disruption acquired remnants in 2020. Cult following — its 'final goodbye' update in 2019 became a viral cultural moment about emotional bonds with robots.

name: Pepper
desc: Iconic humanoid social robot deployed in retail, hospitality and research worldwide. Sold over 20,000 units. SoftBank Robotics halted production in 2021. Aldebaran filed for bankruptcy in 2025, leaving thousands of deployed units without official support.
languages_spoken: 15+ including English, French, Japanese, Mandarin, Spanish

name: NAO
desc: Iconic small humanoid robot used in education, autism therapy, and research worldwide. Over 13,000 units deployed across 70+ countries. Aldebaran's bankruptcy in 2025 halted production though many units remain in active research and educational use.
languages_spoken: 20+ languages including English, French, German, Japanese, Mandarin, Spanish, Arabic

name: Vector 2.0
desc: Revived version of the original Anki Vector after Digital Dream Labs acquired the IP in 2020. Compact desktop companion with personality, voice interaction, Alexa integration, and local processing for privacy.

name: Cozmo
desc: Tabletop personality robot from Anki with expressive facial animations and code-with-Cozmo programming feature. Anki shut down in 2019. Massively influential in the AI-personality category — many of today's social bots draw lineage from Cozmo's design language.

name: Loona
desc: Expressive smart pet robot from Shenzhen-based KEYi Tech. Combines lifelike animations, voice recognition, and emotion-detection AI. Successfully Kickstarted in 2022 raising over $4M, has shipped to 60+ countries.

name: Eilik
desc: Affordable desktop personality robot that went viral via TikTok. Two units can interact and chat with each other. No app, no subscription, no internet required — runs offline with built-in personality scripts.

name: Qoobo
desc: Therapeutic robotic cushion with a moving tail. No face, no voice — just a tail that responds to touch like a cat. Designed for people who can't keep pets (apartments, allergies, eldercare). Won multiple design awards including Red Dot.

name: Hyodol
desc: ChatGPT-powered companion doll deployed at scale in South Korea. Over 12,000 units distributed by Korean municipal governments to elderly living alone. Tracks medication, provides conversation, alerts emergency contacts when issues arise.

name: Abi
desc: AI-powered eldercare companion robot from Melbourne-based Andromeda Robotics. Raised $17M in March 2026 to expand into the US senior care market. Deployed across Australian aged-care homes with focus on cognitive engagement and dignified assistance.

name: NEO
desc: Backed by OpenAI, 1X's NEO is a full-size humanoid designed for home use including companionship and light household assistance. Started shipping to homes in early 2026 at $20,000. Tendon-driven actuation prioritizes safe human-proximate interaction.

name: Ryan
desc: Tabletop social robot from DreamFace Technologies (University of Denver spin-off) featuring an animated face projected onto a translucent 3D head. Used in dementia care research and clinical settings — focused on engaging conversations with cognitively impaired adults.

name: Buddy
desc: Family-oriented social robot from French startup Blue Frog Robotics. Funded via Indiegogo, shipped 2018. Designed to be a household assistant, security monitor, and child companion. Company restructured in 2024 ending consumer sales.

name: Kuri
desc: Family home companion from Mayfield Robotics (a Bosch subsidiary). Cute design with autonomous navigation, no face screen — communicated entirely through eye animations and chirps. Bosch shut down Mayfield in 2018 before mass shipping. All customer deposits were refunded.

name: BDX Droid
desc: Disney's autonomous interactive Star Wars droid character — short for 'Bipedal Dynamic Experiment.' Variants include OSKAR-7 (orange), BESH-27 (blue), GREK-17 (green), Red. Won the 2025 Thea Award for Technical Innovation. Roams Galaxy's Edge at Disneyland, Disney World, Tokyo Disneyland, Disneyland Paris and Shanghai Disneyland. Debuts on screen in The Mandalorian and Grogu (May 2026). Patent filed October 2023 as 'walking robots.'
ai_model: Disney Research autonomous behavior model (RL + Imitation)

name: Project Kiwi (Baby Groot)
desc: Free-walking autonomous Baby Groot character developed by Disney Imagineering as a milestone in expressive character robotics. Pint-sized humanoid with accurately rendered face/hands/feet, distressed red flight suit, expressive eye contact. The Project Kiwi platform later evolved into the BDX droid program. Stages controlled meet-and-greet appearances.

name: Walt Disney – A Magical Life
desc: Audio-Animatronic figure of Walt Disney himself, opened July 17 2025 at Disneyland California for the park's 70th anniversary. Plays in rotation with Great Moments with Mr. Lincoln (1964). 17-minute stage show in the Main Street, USA section. Controversial — Walt's granddaughter Joanna Miller publicly opposed the robot likeness, calling it 'dehumanizing.'
pilot_customers: Disneyland Park, Main Street USA (Disneyland Opera House)

name: ADAM
desc: Dual-armed AI-powered bartender (Automated Dual Arm Mixologist) from NASDAQ-listed Richtech Robotics. Debuted at CES 2024. First robot bartender permanently stationed at a major league sports venue (Texas Rangers Globe Life Field, 2024). Now serving at T-Mobile Arena NHL games. 23-drink menu, NSF certified for food service.
form_factor: Dual-arm robotic torso on counter base
pilot_customers: T-Mobile Arena Las Vegas (NHL Golden Knights)

name: Makr Shakr (Toni)
desc: Two-armed robotic bartender installation co-designed with MIT and Pentagram design studio. Permanently installed on Royal Caribbean's Quantum-class cruise ships, airports, hotels and event spaces worldwide. Compatto model adds coffee; Veloce model can make up to 250 drinks per hour. Pioneered the robotic bartender category.

name: Kuratas
desc: Pilot-operated 4-meter mecha from Japanese artist Kogoro Kurata. Famous for the 2017 international mecha duel against MegaBots Inc.'s Eagle Prime (USA). Available for purchase or rental for events. Combines theatrical scale with a working piloted cockpit. Controlled via Kinect-style motion or smartphone.

name: Stickboy (Compressorhead drummer)
desc: Four-armed pneumatic drummer in the world's first robotic heavy metal band Compressorhead. Built by German engineers from steel auto parts. Has played live across Europe and Australia, opened for Black Sabbath at Wacken Open Air 2016. The full band includes Bones (bass), Fingers (guitar), and Hellga (vocals).

name: Z-Machines
desc: Japanese all-robot band consisting of MACH (78-finger guitarist), ASHURA (22-arm drummer), and COSMO (laser keyboardist). Created by Naofumi Yonetsuka (Tokyo University), performed at SXSW 2013 and Tokyo. Squarepusher composed 'Music for Robots' EP specifically for them in 2014. Project paused after 2015.

name: Blue (Newton-trained BDX)
desc: Fully autonomous BDX-style droid unveiled by Jensen Huang at NVIDIA GTC 2025. Collaboration between NVIDIA, Google DeepMind, and Disney Research. Trained in NVIDIA's Newton physics engine (jointly developed by all three companies) using Isaac GROOT N1 Humanoid Foundation Model. No remote control — fully AI-driven walked on stage with Huang.
ai_model: NVIDIA Isaac GROOT N1 Humanoid Foundation Model

name: Great Moments with Mr. Lincoln
desc: The original full-body Audio-Animatronic figure, debuted at the 1964 New York World's Fair (Illinois Pavilion) and moved to Disneyland in 1965. Has been periodically updated — most recent overhaul 2009 includes more lifelike skin texturing and facial expressions. Foundational milestone of the entire animatronic category, predating Disney's other animatronic shows by decades.
mobility: Static (stands from chair, gestures, hand movements)

name: Bobo and Olive (Sky Force Snack Bar)
desc: Pair of robotic characters serving snacks at the Cosmic Rewind area in Walt Disney World EPCOT. Interact with guests via scripted humorous banter while assisting human cast members. Example of Disney's expansion of robotics from passive animatronics to active service roles.
pilot_customers: Walt Disney World - EPCOT - Guardians of the Galaxy: Cosmic Rewind

name: Shadow Dexterous Hand
desc: Anthropomorphic robotic hand widely used in research, prosthetics development, and entertainment installations. Most human-like robotic hand on the market. Has appeared in art installations including 'In Event of Moon Disaster' at the Imperial War Museum. Used by OpenAI for dexterous manipulation research.

name: Rovio
desc: WiFi-controlled mobile webcam robot from WowWee, designed for home telepresence and remote monitoring. Found a niche in event entertainment as a remotely-operated 'roving reporter' character at conferences and live shows. Discontinued in consumer market.

name: RoboSapien
desc: Mass-market biomorphic robot designed by NASA roboticist Mark Tilden. Sold over 7 million units worldwide making it one of the best-selling robot toys in history. Used in countless trade shows, music videos and entertainment events. Defined the home humanoid toy category and predates almost every modern consumer social robot.

name: Spot (Dancing variant)
desc: Choreographed performance variant of Spot. The viral 'Do You Love Me' video (Dec 2020) reached 30M+ views in a week. Spot units regularly perform at corporate events, sports halftime shows (BTS Korean concert tours), and music videos. Same hardware as standard Spot but with custom Choreographer dance software.

name: Spot
desc: The category-defining commercial quadruped. Released 2019 by Boston Dynamics (then Google/Alphabet, now Hyundai-owned). Used worldwide for industrial inspection, construction site documentation, public safety, research, and entertainment. Over 1,500 units deployed across 30+ countries. Lease price $74,500.

name: Spot Enterprise
desc: Enterprise variant of Spot with self-charging dock, expanded autonomy, and Scout management software. Targets continuous unmanned inspection deployments. Adds 4G LTE option and enhanced safety features over base Spot.

name: Spot with Arm (SpotArm)
desc: Spot equipped with the Boston Dynamics manipulator arm. Adds 7-DOF arm with gripper enabling door-opening, valve-turning, picking up objects, and remote manipulation in hazardous environments. ~$200K total with arm + Spot.

name: Go1
desc: Unitree first-generation Go-series quadruped. Predecessor to Go2. Featured "intelligent side-follow" mode tracking owner via stereo cameras. Mass-market price ($2,700) made it the first sub-$3K quadruped with real autonomy. Largely superseded by Go2 line.

name: ANYmal
desc: Industrial inspection quadruped from ETH Zurich spin-off ANYbotics. Used by BP, Shell, Petronas, and major chemical plants for autonomous routine inspection. IP67 rating, ATEX-compliant Ex-Proof variant available. Now in its D-version (ANYmal D, 2023).

name: CyberDog 2
desc: Xiaomi second-generation consumer quadruped, refined from CyberDog (2021). Bio-mimetic Doberman-inspired design. Open-source platform with NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX, AI vision (face/gesture/voice recognition), and developer SDK. Targets developers and tech-enthusiast consumers.
cameras: AI camera + Intel RealSense D430 depth + ultra-wide fish-eye

name: X50 Ultra
desc: Dreame's 2025 flagship robot vacuum unveiled at CES 2025. First with ProLeap System retractable legs to climb 6cm thresholds. 20,000 Pa suction, retracting LiDAR (89mm low profile under furniture), HyperStream Detangling DuoBrush, hot-water mop washing.

name: X40 Ultra
desc: Mid-2024 Dreame flagship before the X50 Ultra. First Dreame with extendable, lifting side brush as standard. All-rubber floating brush with optional TriCut anti-tangle. 12,000 Pa suction, sonic vibrating mop pads, hot-water self-cleaning dock.

name: X40 Master
desc: Premium X40 variant with enhanced AI obstacle avoidance and additional dock features. Same 12,000 Pa suction and lifting side brush as X40 Ultra.

name: L40 Ultra Gen 2
desc: Refreshed L40 Ultra with 25,000 Pa suction (massive upgrade), DuoScrub mopping, 100-day self-empty cycle, multifunctional PowerDock. Mid-range flagship aimed at homes with pets.

name: L50 Ultra
desc: Brings the X50's ProLeap threshold-crossing feature to a more affordable L-series tier. 19,500 Pa suction, 60mm (2.36 inch) obstacle crossing.

name: D10s Plus
desc: Mid-tier Dreame with self-empty base, LiDAR navigation, and dual-mode mop. Strong value pick under $400.

name: Deebot X8 Pro Omni
desc: Ecovacs 2025 flagship — first Ecovacs with OZMO Roller continuous-rinse roller mop. 18,000 Pa suction, AIVI 3D 3.0 AI obstacle recognition, TruEdge 2.0 extending edge cleaning, ZeroTangle 2.0 anti-tangle. Hot-water 40-75°C mop washing + 63°C drying.

name: Deebot X2 Omni
desc: Ecovacs square-design flagship of 2024. Unique square shape for better corner reach. 8,000 Pa suction, dual spinning mop pads with auto-lift, AIVI 3D obstacle avoidance.

name: Deebot T50 Pro Omni
desc: T-series flagship 2025 with 15,000 Pa suction. Re-Mop function for stain recognition and targeted re-mopping.

name: X10 Pro Omni
desc: Eufy/Anker's flagship 2024 robot vacuum. 8,000 Pa suction, dual spinning mop pads with 1 kg pressure, auto-lift on carpet. Omni dock with hot-water washing and drying.

name: Omni E25
desc: Eufy 2025 step-up with Omni multi-function dock. 8,000 Pa suction, dual spinning mop with detergent dosing.

name: Roomba Max 10
desc: iRobot 2025 flagship — first Roomba with LiDAR navigation (a major shift from longstanding vSLAM-only approach). 70× more suction than the original Roomba. Dual-roller PerfectEdge brushes.

name: Jet Bot AI+
desc: Samsung's premium vacuum-only flagship. Object recognition AI co-developed with Intel. Clean Station auto-empty dock. SmartThings integration including remote camera viewing through robot.

name: Bespoke Jet Bot Combo
desc: Samsung 2024 vacuum-mop combo. Steam mop sterilization (200 Pa steam pressure), full self-empty + mop wash + dry station, AI Object Recognition 2.0.

name: Matrix Plus 2-in-1
desc: Shark's matrix-cleaning vacuum-mop hybrid. Multi-pass overlapping matrix cleaning pattern, sonic mop scrubbing, self-empty XL base.

name: S10
desc: Unique direct-plumbing robot vacuum — connects to home water supply and drainage for unlimited continuous mopping. 6,500 Pa suction, roller mop, no manual water filling required.

name: Floor One S7 Combo
desc: Tineco's foray into robot vacuums — pairs a robot vacuum with the company's well-known cordless wet-dry vacuums in a single combo.

name: Robot Vacuum X20+
desc: Xiaomi's flagship 2023 robot vacuum and mop. 7,000 Pa suction, dual spinning mop pads with 18 N pressure, auto-lift on carpet, LDS LiDAR navigation. Self-empty + mop wash + mop dry station.
mop_type: Dual spinning with auto-lift (18 N pressure)

name: Robot Vacuum X20 Max
desc: Step-up X20 with 10,000 Pa suction and enhanced AI obstacle avoidance. AI 3D dToF navigation, dual edge brushes.

name: Robot Vacuum S20+
desc: Mid-tier Xiaomi vacuum with 5,000 Pa suction, vibration mop, and self-empty base. Strong sub-$400 value.

name: S9 UV
desc: Viomi's premium robot vacuum with UV sterilization. 2,700 Pa suction, self-empty dock, electronically-controlled mopping with three water flow levels.

name: Alpha UV+
desc: Viomi mid-range robovac with UV sterilization. Predecessor to the S9 UV.

name: A10s
desc: iLife budget-friendly LiDAR robot vacuum. 2,000 Pa suction, no-mop, accurate mapping. Popular among low-budget buyers seeking real LiDAR (not just gyro nav).

name: V9e
desc: iLife low-cost gyroscope-navigation vacuum. Targets sub-$200 segment.

name: S7 Pro
desc: Tesvor mid-range LiDAR vacuum-mop with 4000 Pa suction. Popular sub-$300 Amazon option.

name: Emma
desc: Trifo focuses on robot vacuums with AI cameras and home-security cruise mode. Used as both cleaner and indoor patrol/security camera.

name: Lucy
desc: Earlier Trifo with home-security patrol features. Dual-camera setup, AI obstacle recognition.

name: S10 Ultra
desc: 3i (Hong Kong-based startup) premium robot vacuum-mop with self-empty + auto mop wash. 12,000 Pa suction, popular launch via crowdfunding.

name: Wyze Robot Vacuum
desc: Wyze's budget-friendly entry into the LiDAR vacuum space. Real LiDAR navigation at sub-$250, no mopping. Strong value pick.

name: Tapo RV30 Plus
desc: TP-Link's Tapo smart-home brand robot vacuum. 4,200 Pa suction, real LiDAR navigation, self-empty base. Competitive mid-tier under $400.

name: SL60D
desc: Lubluelu budget LiDAR vacuum-mop combo. 3,000 Pa suction, popular Amazon Prime Day discounter under $200.

name: M1
desc: Mova (Dreame sub-brand) value-tier robot vacuum-mop. 7,000 Pa suction, dual spinning mop, full self-empty + wash + dry station at competitive price.

name: Scuba S1
desc: Aiper's flagship cordless robotic pool cleaner. Cleans floors + walls + waterline. WavePath 2.0 navigation, 5-hour runtime per charge. CES 2024 Innovation Award winner.

name: Seagull Pro
desc: Mid-range Aiper cordless pool cleaner. Floor-only cleaning, 2.5-hour runtime, sub-$700 price point.

name: Z1 Pro (Pool)
desc: Dreame's pool-cleaner entry. Cordless, wall-climbing, waterline cleaning. Smart pathing with Dreame app integration.

name: AquaSense Pro
desc: Premium AI-powered pool cleaner. 5-in-1 cleaning (floor/walls/waterline/water surface/clarification). Best-in-class app and clean pattern intelligence.

name: Winbot W2 Omni
desc: Ecovacs window-cleaning robot with portable battery dock. Cordless freedom — operates on windows without a fixed plug. AI cleaning path planning.

name: Winbot Mini
desc: Compact Ecovacs window cleaner unveiled at CES 2025. Smaller form factor for tight spaces and smaller windows.

name: A2 Ultra
desc: Top-tier A2 flagship. 40 DOF, dexterous 6-DoF hands, 3D LiDAR + RGB-D + RGB/fisheye sensor suite. Multi-region certified (China, US, Europe). Designed for interactive services and high-endurance walking — proven by 106km Guinness-certified walk.

name: A2 Max
desc: Heavy-duty industrial variant of A2. 175cm, 85kg with 67 DOF, 40kg dual-arm payload, 450 N·m torque, 8800N leg thrust. Demoed lifting 40kg aviation box. Designed for material handling and palletizing in industrial/warehousing.

name: LUBA 2 AWD 10000H
desc: Top-tier LUBA 2 for 2.5-acre lawns. Same chassis, slope-handling, and AI Vision as 5000H but with doubled battery for 2x daily coverage. Best for large properties up to ~10,000m². Industry-leading 80%/38° slope.
use_cases: Large residential & light commercial lawns to 2.5 acres

name: Terra Robot Mower
desc: iRobot's robot lawn mower project, announced 2018 but cancelled in February 2020 during COVID-era restructuring. Used beacon-based 'Smart Bladed Mower' technology. Never reached mass production. Historic reference.

name: Omni S1 Pro
desc: Eufy/Anker flagship 2024 launched via Kickstarter ($3.5M raised from 3,200 backers). World's first HydroJet roller mop system — spinning roller at 170 RPM continuously rinses itself with ozonated water, processing liquid into onboard dirty-water tank. 10-in-1 UniClean Station handles auto-empty, wash, refill, drying, ozone sanitization. 8,000 Pa suction, 3D MatrixEye obstacle avoidance, 12.7mm mop auto-lift.

name: C28
desc: Eufy mid-flagship 2025 — brings HydroJet roller mop down-market. 15,000 Pa suction, Always-Fresh roller mop, zero-tangle design, auto wash + dry. Upgraded from X10 Pro.

name: E25
desc: Eufy 2025 mid-range with 20,000 Pa suction, HydroJet roller mop, edge-to-corner cleaning, zero-tangle. Strong value at sub-$700.

name: Conga X150
desc: Cecotec 2025 flagship unveiled at IFA 2025. Spanish brand's top-tier robot vacuum. 25,000 Pa suction (one of highest in market), two rotating mop discs, anti-hair-tangle system, laser navigation. Cecotec is the #1 home appliance brand in Spain.

name: Conga Z150
desc: Cecotec Conga Z150 with extended roller mop design. Sister flagship to X150 with different mopping system architecture.

name: Conga X80
desc: Cecotec X-series mid-tier with two rotating mop discs and anti-hair-tangle system. Predecessor to X150.

name: Conga Z100 X-Treme
desc: Mid-2024 Cecotec with 20,000 Pa, AI artificial intelligence, professional scrubbing, XXL bi-material mop, self-empty station.

name: Conga Y50 X-Treme
desc: Cecotec Y-series with self-emptying base, laser navigation, 5,000 Pa, 3L tank.

name: Conga 9990 AI
desc: Cecotec mid-flagship with AI navigation, self-empty + mop wash station. Popular Spanish-market pick under €800.

name: S10 Pro
desc: 360 (Qihoo) robotics arm produces mid-range robot vacuums popular in Asia. S10 Pro with 3,300 Pa suction, LiDAR navigation, dual-mop system.

name: S9
desc: 360 Robot earlier-gen LiDAR vacuum with vibration mop. Sub-$350 LiDAR option.

name: Scuba X1
desc: Aiper's 2025 flagship pool cleaner. Wall + waterline + floor cleaning, 8-hour runtime, AI-powered WavePath 3.0 navigation. CES 2025 Innovation Award.

name: Seagull 2000
desc: Aiper entry-level cordless pool cleaner. Floor-only cleaning, 90-minute runtime, under $400 price.

name: Orca 3000
desc: Aiper mid-tier cordless pool cleaner. Floor + waterline cleaning, 3-hour runtime, smart navigation.

name: M12 Pro+
desc: Yeedi (Ecovacs subsidiary) 2024 flagship with 11,000 Pa suction, dual oscillating mop pads with 15N pressure, AI obstacle avoidance, self-empty + auto mop wash station.

name: Cube Pro
desc: Yeedi 2025 cubic flagship — integrated station design with hot water mop washing. 11,000 Pa suction.

name: X1 Combo Pro
desc: Proscenic flagship with self-empty + mop wash, 5,000 Pa suction, full omni-station functionality at sub-$700.

name: T10 Elite
desc: Ultenic budget-tier with full self-empty + mop wash station, 5,500 Pa suction. Popular Amazon mid-range pick.

name: Mop Station Pro
desc: Yeedi mop-focused robot with self-washing station. No vacuuming — dedicated mopping platform for tile/wood homes.

name: NoMo Q11
desc: Neabot early self-emptying budget vacuum. Strong Amazon seller before bigger brands captured the segment.

name: Qrevo Edge
desc: Roborock Qrevo Edge with FlexiArm Arc extending side brush and mop. 18,500 Pa suction, dual brushes, hot-water mop wash.

name: L9000
desc: Tikom budget LiDAR vacuum-mop. Strong Amazon seller in sub-$300 segment.

name: Q6 Pro
desc: Honiture budget LiDAR vacuum-mop. Popular sub-$250 Amazon pick.

name: S8 MaxV Ultra
desc: Roborock 2024 flagship — 10,000 Pa suction, voice assistant 'Rocky', VibraRise 3.0 sonic mopping, FlexiArm extending side brush. Reactive AI 2.0 obstacle recognition.
mop_type: VibraRise 3.0 sonic vibrating + spinning side mop
